title: Exchange functoriality: naturality, identities, and pasting
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], with $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of finite-type $k$-schemes whose arrows are separated and of finite type. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ put $K'=Lg'^*K$ and form
$$\operatorname{Ex}_*(K):Lg^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*K',\qquad \operatorname{Ex}_!(K):Lg^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!K'.$$
The coefficient categories and these symbols have the following typing. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ use bounded-below constant-coefficient module categories on the small étale sites and their pro-étale transports on complexes supplied with étale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ use the derived-complete pro-étale categories, with $Lg^*$ denoting completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and compatible étale-origin witnesses on all finite reductions when compact support or smooth base change is invoked. At $\Lambda=E$ use raw scalar localization of the completed integral categories and functors, with the localized integral exchange as in [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change]; at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use common finite stages. Retain the specified lattice presentations, constructibility and amplitude hypotheses of [thm-cbc-finite-extension], [thm-cbc-qbar] and of the smooth-base-change statements below. Assertions in $D^b_c$ are restrictions of the ambient assertions whenever the displayed operations preserve that subcategory; no preservation is implicit in this notation.

At finite étale level $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is the constant-module unit--square--counit mate of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]; at witnessed finite pro-étale level it is the mate of [def-exchange-projection], equivalently the constant-ring mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], identified with the étale map in the proof; $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is the compactification formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map], transported by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] on the witnessed pro-étale domain. At the integral stage use the completed adjunction-mate exchange and the compact-support map of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Integral open factors are reconstructed from their strict finite extension-by-zero reduction diagrams as in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; in constant-coefficient coordinates they are $J_j^c=CJ_j$, with the normalization proved below. At field coefficients use their rational and common-stage transports. Then:

1. Both transformations are natural in $K$. They respect morphisms of square data through the canonical functor comparison transformations: taking a mate commutes with pre- and post-whiskering of the square comparison. They commute with coefficient comparisons on the domains of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; finite quotient comparisons for compact support use the stated finite-Tor domains. The compact-support map agrees with [def-cbc-exchange-map], [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], [thm-cbc-finite-extension] and [thm-cbc-qbar] at their respective stages.
2. For an identity base change the transformations are identities under the canonical identity-functor comparisons. For horizontally pasted squares $(f,f',g,g')$, $(f',f'',h,h')$, writing $P$ for either $R(-)_*$ or $R(-)_!$, the equation is
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{gh}=(\operatorname{Ex}_h\,Lg'^*)\circ(Lh^*\operatorname{Ex}_g).$$
For vertically pasted squares $(f,f',g,g')$, $(e,e',g',g'')$ it is
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{fe}=(P(f')\operatorname{Ex}_e)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_f P(e)).$$
These equations insert the canonical pullback and direct-image composition isomorphisms, and for compact support the finite-level composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and its completed and transported forms constructed in the proof. At finite étale level they are exactly the formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], [sbc-lem-identity-and-base-change-composition] for $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ and [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$; the same equations hold on the completed and transported domains above.
3. If $g$ is smooth, then $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is the smooth-base-change map with the labels exchanged, as defined in [sbc-def-base-change-map], and is an isomorphism. At finite étale level this is [sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change]; on witnessed finite pro-étale complexes use [sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change]. At integral, rational and algebraically closed rational levels retain respectively the coefficient and lattice hypotheses of [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change], [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change], and [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch], including finite dimension of the input and output corners $X$ and $Y'$, the chosen lattice presentation at $E$, and their uniform-interval hypotheses when asserting the result in $D^b_c$. Finite dimension here follows from finite type over $k$, as verified in the proof. The displayed exchange functors have their codomain on $Y'$.
4. The compact-support transformation is independent of the compactification, commutes with the refinement comparisons of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] on its witnessed domain, and is compatible with the finite-level composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and its completed and transported forms on the corresponding coefficient domains.

proof.text:
Fix a finite coefficient ring. At the finite etale level use the specified constant-module mate of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] and the compactification formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. For a compactification $f=pj$ they give
$$\operatorname{Ex}_*=R f'_*(Lg'^*\varepsilon_f)\circ R f'_*(\theta Rf_*)\circ\eta_{f'},\qquad \operatorname{Ex}_!^c=Rp'_*\beta\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}(j_!-).$$
The open-factor map $\beta$ is natural, has identity normalization and satisfies pasting by [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. At finite pro-etale level [def-exchange-projection] explicitly defines these same unit--square--counit and proper-plus-open composites in the ambient constant-module categories. Its compactification superscript records a choice and its definition assumes no compactification coherence; Step 2 compares the etale and pro-etale formulas on the witnessed domain, and Steps 10–15 prove the needed coherence. Naturality of each unit, counit, square comparison and $\beta$ implies naturality of the displayed composites in $K$.

source.place: Proof Step 1 and first part of Step 2; Stacks 07A7, remark-base-change, and 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change

proof.text: For finite pro-étale coefficients use the specified mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. The normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] says precisely $T_L\nu^*(E_L)=\operatorname{Ex}^{R}_{\nu^*L}S_L$; therefore the étale and pro-étale ordinary exchanges agree under the canonical comparisons, rather than under an arbitrary choice of isomorphism. For compact support, [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] specifies the transported map of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. All these comparisons are natural; a change of witness by an isomorphism conjugates both endpoints and the map, so gives the same transformation on the witnessed domain. The qcqs hypotheses of the direct-image comparison hold: by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] finite type includes quasi-compactness, while separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine and quasi-compact; thus $f$ and $f'$ are quasi-separated. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$), and its spectrum is one point; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to the four structure morphisms therefore makes every corner Noetherian. [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] applied over $k$ makes every corner finite-dimensional. These verifications do not use smoothness and supply the geometric category domains also needed in Steps 17–20. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact; intersections of affine opens are open subsets of a Noetherian affine scheme and hence quasi-compact, so it is quasi-separated. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications of each separated finite-type edge and of the composites used below. Their ambient schemes are proper over finite-type k-schemes, hence finite type over k and again Noetherian and finite-dimensional by the same two cited results.

source.place: Proof Steps 1 and 2, finite-site transport; explicit distinction of the étale-origin domain

proof.text: Set $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\varpi_E)$. [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives the DVR and uniformizer, so $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}A]$ in degrees $-1,0$ resolves $P_n$. [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] gives finite quotients. The residue characteristic is $\ell$: $|\ell|_E<1$, whereas an integer prime to $\ell$ is a unit. The successive uniformizer quotients are copies of the residue field, so each $P_n$ is killed by a power of $\ell$ and $A/I$ is additive torsion. These checks establish every perfect/torsion/finite coefficient hypothesis used below. [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies the complete categories, finite reductions, strict quotient transitions, derived limits and completion units between constant and completed sheaves. [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identifies the named integral pullback with $Cu^*$ in these coordinates.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies the completed-sheaf direct image with constant-coefficient direct image, with its specified K-injective/composite normalization, strict coefficient transitions and limit projections. Its primes are our $p=\operatorname{char}k$ and $\ell$, distinct by hypothesis, and its schemes may be arbitrary. Together with the unit-preserving coefficient equivalence this fixes the right adjoint; the hom-set bijections of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] fix its adjunction with $Cu^*$. Thus all subsequent constant-coefficient calculations transport to the named completed operations, with their units and counits.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison] with $B=G_gR_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_XK$, $D=R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}G_{g'}\mathcal R_XK$, and $v=E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathcal R_XK}$. Its specified comparisons satisfy $tE^c=R\lim(v)s$, so the completed mate is $t^{-1}R\lim(v)s$. Perfection was checked above; this comparison imposes no flatness on a scheme map. For a proper factor $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization] gives $d\operatorname{Res}(v')=vb$ for the actual strict lift used by [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. The comparisons $b,d$ use the same restriction and diagram projection-formula maps. Apply $R\lim$ to that equality and conjugate by these source and target maps: the proper completed factor is precisely $E^c$. This identifies the maps before evaluating at any level.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: For the open factor apply [lem-sf-cbc-extension-zero-completion]. It supplies $J_j^c=CJ_j$, the actual strict reduction isomorphism $q_j:\mathcal R(J_j^cK)\cong J_j\mathcal R(K)$, its completion-unit normalization, and the specified presentation $J_j^cK\cong R\lim J_j\mathcal R(K)$. Finite witnesses are $j_!L_n$ through its stated site comparison; no transitions between those witnesses are invented. Hence the canonical direct-image/limit comparison [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] identifies $Rp_*J_j^cK$ with $R\lim(R_p^{\mathcal T}J_j\mathcal R K)$, exactly the tower construction of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The proper factor acts on the complete object $J_j^cK$ and the open exchange is $R\lim$ of the strict open comparison. This is the ordered proper-plus-open map of [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], with the open normalization supplied by [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] on its compatible-origin domain. No commutation of ordinary $J_j$ with infinite limits is used.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text:
For changes of the square comparisons, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] gives the precise naturality equation
$$\operatorname{mate}((\tau L_1)\alpha(L_2\sigma))=(R_2\tau)\operatorname{mate}(\alpha)(\sigma R_1).$$
Consequently the unit--square--counit formula respects a compatible morphism of square data, with its comparison maps inserted. For coefficient change, [lem-fix-operation-reduction] states that the supplied comparisons preserve the units and counits constructing exchange; it includes the finite-Tor qualification for finite quotient compact-support comparisons. Substituting these unit, square and counit comparisons in the displayed mate formula gives a commuting comparison square. For finite field extensions the ordinary-exchange comparison is explicitly part of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For the compactification formula apply the same substitution to the proper factor and the extension-by-zero comparison; preservation of compositions gives the compact-support comparison. This asserts compatibility only for these specified coefficient comparisons, not commutation of arbitrary scalar extension with arbitrary direct image.

source.place: Proof Step 2, precise morphism-of-square and coefficient-comparison interpretation

proof.text: For ordinary identity and pasting, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies finite composition termwise. On tensor generators both associations send $r\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $rs\otimes x$, and the identity sends $1\otimes x$ to $x$. Thus the outer pullback-square identification is the pasted identification. At completed coefficients take the direct-image comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and their adjunction conjugates under [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. For three adjunctions the composite hom-set bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] composes the same three functions in the same order. Associativity of function composition and injectivity of the conjugacy bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] therefore give associativity and identity of the normalized completed comparisons. This is a normalization argument for the specified adjunctions, not an additional base-change theorem.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: Apply clauses (1),(2),(3),(4) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to these square comparisons and composition conjugacies. They give respectively horizontal pasting, vertical pasting and identity for $\operatorname{Ex}_*$, with exactly the equations displayed in the statement. This applies to the finite and completed adjunctions. The finite etale normalizations are those in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] and [sbc-lem-identity-and-base-change-composition].

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: For compact support at finite étale level, [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] states naturality, identity normalization, both pasting laws, independence of compactification, and compatibility with the proper/open comparisons. One can see the compatibility with a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ directly in the formula: [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] gives the commuting base-change square for $Ru_*j_{1!}\cong j_{2!}$. Whisker this square by the direct images of the proper compactification factors and insert the ordinary vertical-pasting equation of Steps 8–9. Its two boundary composites are precisely $\operatorname{Ex}^{c_1}_!$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^{c_2}_!$ conjugated by the refinement maps. These refinement maps and their cocycle are exactly [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] on the witnessed pro-étale domain. Comparing two compactifications through a common refinement, the commuting squares just proved and the cocycle show equality after either comparison; no choice of common refinement remains. Finite pro-étale transport carries this equality to the domain of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale].

proof.text: For the integral refinement and composition argument put $N=\mathcal R_XK$ in constant $A$-coefficient diagram categories. Use [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison] for $\Gamma_Q:J_iR_r^{\mathcal T}\to R_p^{\mathcal T}J_k$, normalized by $\lambda_QG_i\Gamma_Q=1$. Its statement identifies this with the finite proper/open map on every witnessed level. [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] supplies its base-change equation and both composition equations as actual derived diagram transformations: the calculus's $\gamma_Q$ equals $\Gamma_Q$ because both have the open-adjunction normalization stated in [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison]. This replaces the long inline proper/open coherence verification. All open maps here are quasi-compact since their ambient schemes are Noetherian. Each $J_jN_n$ has witness $j_!L_n$ by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]; exactness of the open functors [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] gives the same comparison on bounded-below complexes. Thus the calculus's finite-origin hypotheses hold without any uniform bound in $n$.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text:
For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ take the commuting proper/open square $Q_u=(r=1_X,p=u,k=j_1,i=j_2)$, allowed by [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison]. Its $\Gamma_{Q_u}$ is invertible on $N$. Define
$$\rho_u:R_{p_1}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_1}N\cong R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}R_u^{\mathcal T}J_{j_1}N\xrightarrow{R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\Gamma_{Q_u}^{-1}}R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_2}N.$$
Its evaluations are [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Whisker the base-change equation of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] by $R_{p'_2}^{\mathcal T}$ and insert [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for the proper factors. With $E_i=R_{p'_i}^{\mathcal T}\beta_{j_i}\circ E_{p_i}J_{j_i}$, the resulting boundary equation is $\rho_{u'}G_{g'}\circ E_1=E_2\circ G_g\rho_u$. The calculus's identity and composition equations give identity and transitivity of $\rho$. Common refinements and their cocycle are provided by [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]; hence the comparison is independent of the refinement chosen.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text:
For composition choose compactifications $d=(v,b)$ of $f:Y\to S$ and $c_0$ of $fe:X\to S$ as supplied in Step 2. [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] with $(e,f,d,c_0)$ gives $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, with $a=tc$, $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $t:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p_Y:V\to Y$ proper. For $Q=(r=p_Y,p=p,k=t,i=v)$ define in diagram categories
$$\alpha^{\mathcal T}_{f,e}:R_b^{\mathcal T}J_vR_{p_Y}^{\mathcal T}J_c\xrightarrow{R_b^{\mathcal T}\Gamma_QJ_c}R_b^{\mathcal T}R_p^{\mathcal T}J_tJ_c\cong R_{bp}^{\mathcal T}J_{tc}.$$
The proper/open isomorphism is [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison]. The evaluations are the specified finite composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition]; that theorem preserves the bounded-below etale-origin class, so both successive compact-support operations are in its domain. The field, invertible prime, positive index and separated finite-type maps are our standing data.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text:
For the two vertically stacked base-change squares, the equation in the diagram category is
$$E_{fe}\circ G_g\alpha^{\mathcal T}_{f,e}=(\alpha^{\mathcal T}_{f',e'}G_{g''})\circ(F_{f'}E_e)\circ(E_fF_e),$$
where $F$ is the proper/open compactification composite on towers. Expanding the three factors defining $\alpha^{\mathcal T}$, the proper/open rectangle is the base-change equation of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], the proper-composition rectangle is [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], and the open-composition rectangle is the open-composition clause of that calculus. Pasting these three commuting rectangles proves the displayed equation before applying $R\lim$. The same calculus gives the horizontal and identity equations and compatibility under refinement. Thus no equality of derived diagram morphisms is inferred merely from their finite evaluations.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text:
Use [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit] to identify every nested completed operation in these diagrams with the derived limit of the corresponding strict word. Its open generator is the normalized $J_j^c$ already fixed above; its proper generator uses the tower projection formula and direct-image/limit map. Hence the middle vertex has the same specified comparison in both adjacent arrows. [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison] identifies every proper exchange with its completed mate, and [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] identifies the ordered compact-support composite. Apply the exact functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to the refinement and composition equations. If $a_i:C_i\cong R\lim V_i$ are the specified vertex maps and $U:V_0\to V_1$, $V:V_1\to V_2$, the completed arrows compose as
$$a_2^{-1}R\lim(V)a_1\,a_1^{-1}R\lim(U)a_0=a_2^{-1}R\lim(VU)a_0.$$
Thus the integral equations hold with the required $\alpha$ normalization, identity and refinement independence. No completeness of ordinary extension by zero or faithfulness of evaluations is used.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: For rational coefficients [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] extends functors and natural transformations by scalar localization. Explicitly an integral equality of composites becomes the same equality after tensoring each morphism with $1$; this preserves naturality, identity, both pasting equations and the refinement and composition squares. For compact support, all four corners are Noetherian and finite-dimensional by Step 2, $\ell$ is invertible on them, and $f$ is separated of finite type. Thus the current statement of [thm-cbc-finite-extension] applies to every $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$ on its raw rationalized completed categories. It explicitly defines its exchange as the extension of the specified completed integral exchange, so the map is exactly ours; it is independent of the integral representative and natural for every rational morphism. The current statement imposes no additional lattice-reduction interval hypothesis for this compact-support conclusion. The separate lattice and common-interval qualifications used for smooth ordinary exchange remain those of Steps 17–20. For algebraically closed rational coefficients [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] descends compatible transformations and their equations. Represent the finitely many objects and arrows in any one of our diagrams at a common finite extension, prove the equality there as just done, and use its class in the common-stage category; enlarging the stage preserves the equation by the scalar comparisons of Step 7. [thm-cbc-qbar] identifies this map with the stipulated compact-support exchange and asserts independence of the representative. This proves clauses (1), (2), (4) at the remaining coefficient stages.

source.place: Proof Steps 2, 3 and 5, rationalization and common-stage transports

proof.text:
For the smooth assertion relabel $S_{\rm sbc}=Y$, $X_{\rm sbc}=Y'$, $T_{\rm sbc}=X$, $Y_{\rm sbc}=X'$, and $(f_{\rm sbc},g_{\rm sbc},h_{\rm sbc},e_{\rm sbc})=(g,f,f',g')$. [sbc-def-base-change-map] states that its finite exchange has transpose
$$Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{Lg'^*\varepsilon_f}Lg'^*K.$$
This is exactly the mate defining our $\operatorname{Ex}_*$. At integral coefficients use [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison], not the finite etale definition: its equation $tE^c=R\lim(v)s$ identifies the finite-diagram construction with the named completed mate, with the fixed adjunction of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. The coefficient equivalences and the direct-image comparison above retain these units and counits. Thus the smooth map identification is an equality of the specified maps.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: At finite etale coefficients every cohomology sheaf of $K$ is killed by a power of $\ell$, invertible on the base. The direct-image edge $f$ is qcqs by Step 2 and the other base edge $g$ is smooth. Apply [sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change] after forgetting module coefficients. [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies the forgotten map with the specified abelian-sheaf exchange and detects invertibility. For a finite pro-etale witness $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] gives $T_L\nu^*(E_L)=\operatorname{Ex}^{R}_{\nu^*L}S_L$. Both comparison maps are isomorphisms, so the witnessed exchange is invertible. This covers every bounded-below witness in the reduction tower. [sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change] gives the bounded constructible specialization only on its stated domain.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: Every evaluation of the actual tower mate $v$ is the finite coefficient mate by [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison], hence is invertible by the preceding step. The cone of $v$ has zero evaluated cohomology. Kernels and cokernels of diagram sheaves are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so that cone is acyclic and $v$ is invertible in the derived diagram category. The functor $R\lim$ preserves this isomorphism, and invertible $s,t$ give invertibility of the specified completed mate $E^c=t^{-1}R\lim(v)s$. This proves the ambient integral assertion. [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] supplies its stated bounded-constructible restriction when its common-interval hypotheses hold. All corners are Noetherian and finite-dimensional by Step 2; the finite coefficient hypotheses were checked above, so no new geometric assumption is needed.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–5, expanded along the original split route

proof.text: At $E$, apply [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] to the specified finite-level etale admissible lattice $L$ and presentation $L[1/\varpi]\cong K_E$. It explicitly localizes the integral completed operations and exchange, so its map is ours and is invertible in the ambient category on the output $Y'$. Square-constructible admissibility is used only for the additional $D^b_c(Y',E)$ conclusion. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch] assumes the corresponding hypotheses on every finite representative and their common-overfield passages, and represents its exchange by the same finite-stage map. The common-stage transport above therefore identifies it with ours. In each convention the smooth base map is $g$ and the output corner is $Y'$. The current integral and algebraically closed statements already have the correct output index; the obsolete typo commentary in the previous split is no longer needed.
